{{Use British English|date=September 2012}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=February 2021}}
[[File:The 2007 Carling Cup.jpg|thumb|The winner of the final receives the eponymous [[EFL Cup]].|alt=The Football League Cup on display.]]
The [[EFL Cup]] is a [[Single-elimination tournament|knockout]] cup competition in [[Football in England|English football]] organised by and named after the [[English Football League]] (EFL).<ref name="history">{{cite web |url=http://www.carlingcup.premiumtv.co.uk/page/History/0,,11995,00.html |title=The History of the League Cup |access-date=22 October 2008 |work=Football League Cup |publisher=[[Coors Brewing Company]] |archive-date=23 December 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121223190248/http://www.carling.com/football/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> The competition was established in 1960 and is considered to be the second-most important domestic cup competition for English football clubs, after the [[FA Cup]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2008/jan/23/carlingcup0708 |first=Barney |last=Ronay |title=Why Everton or Spurs must win the Carling Cup |work=The Guardian |date=23 January 2008 |access-date=19 January 2009 |location=London }}</ref> The competition is open to all 72 members of the [[English Football League]] and the 20 members of the [[Premier League]]. For the first six seasons of the competition, the final was contested over [[Two-legged match|two legs]], one at each participating club's stadium. The first Football League Cup was won by [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]], who beat [[Rotherham United F.C.|Rotherham United]] 3–2 on [[Two-legged tie|aggregate]], after losing the first leg 2–0. The competition's first single-legged final was held in 1967: [[Queens Park Rangers F.C.|Queens Park Rangers]] defeated [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] 3–2 at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]] in London.<ref name="history"/>

As of 2026, 24 clubs have won the EFL Cup. [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] hold the record for the most EFL Cup titles, with ten victories in the competition. Liverpool's wins include four consecutive titles from 1981 to 1984, while [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s, who have won nine times, include four consecutive titles from 2018 to 2021. [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] and [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] are the only other clubs to have won consecutive titles. Forest won two consecutive titles twice – in 1978 and 1979, and 1989 and 1990, while United won consecutive editions in 2009 and 2010. [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] have been runners-up more than any other club; they have lost the final seven times. The current holders are Manchester City, who beat Arsenal 2–0 in the [[2026 EFL Cup final|2026 final]] to win their ninth League Cup.

==History==
{{details|EFL Cup}}
The first winners of the tournament were [[Aston Villa F.C.|Aston Villa]]. The final was contested over two legs for the first six years of the competition. During this period many [[Football League First Division|First Division]] clubs refused to take part, allowing clubs from outside the First Division to regularly reach the final. The first club from outside the First Division to win the competition was [[Norwich City F.C.|Norwich City]] of the [[Football League Second Division|Second Division]] in 1962. [[Queen's Park Rangers F.C.|Queen's Park Rangers]] and [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]], both then of Division Three, matched this feat in 1967 and 1969 respectively. [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]], then in the Second Division, became the last club to win the competition while competing outside the First Division, when they beat Manchester United in the [[1991 Football League Cup final|1991 final]].<ref name="history"/>

In the late 1960s, the winners of the competition were granted automatic qualification to the [[UEFA Cup]].<ref name="league">{{cite web |url=http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/CarlingCupDetail/0,,10794%7E475424,00.html |title=League Cup History |work=football-league.co.uk |publisher=The Football League |access-date=8 January 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090106134758/http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/CarlingCupDetail/0%2C%2C10794~475424%2C00.html |archive-date=6 January 2009}}</ref> With the promise of potential European football, First Division clubs entered the competition, and all 92 Football League clubs entered the League Cup for the first time in [[1969–70 Football League Cup|1969–70]]. Meanwhile, the final of the competition had also been altered; it would now be played over a single leg at [[Wembley Stadium (1923)|Wembley Stadium]]. The final went to a replay for the first time in 1977, with Aston Villa requiring two replays to overcome [[Everton F.C.|Everton]]; the first was held at [[Hillsborough Stadium]] in [[Sheffield]], and the second at [[Old Trafford]] in Manchester.<ref name="history"/>

The following year, [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] won the first of two consecutive titles, the first time that any club won back-to-back League Cup titles. The first took a replay at Old Trafford to beat [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]], and they beat [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]] 3–2 to win the second. Liverpool won four consecutive titles between 1981 and 1984, a record equalled by Manchester City in 2021. Nottingham Forest won two more consecutive titles in 1989 and 1990.<ref name="league"/>

The last League Cup final replay was held in 1997; [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]] beat [[Middlesbrough F.C.|Middlesbrough]] 1–0 after [[extra time]] at Hillsborough, after the two clubs had played out a 1–1 draw at Wembley. The rules were changed afterwards with a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] incorporated instead of replays.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/LeagueCupPastWinners/0,,10794~1354853,00.html |title=League Cup Past Winners |work=football-league.co.uk |publisher=The Football League |access-date=8 January 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203092702/http://www.football-league.co.uk/page/LeagueCupPastWinners/0%2C%2C10794~1354853%2C00.html |archive-date= 3 December 2013 }}</ref> The first single-match final to be played outside London was held in 2001, as the final was moved to [[Cardiff]]'s [[Millennium Stadium]] while the new [[Wembley Stadium]] was under construction.<ref name="history"/> Liverpool and [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] were the two most prolific League Cup sides in Cardiff, as both clubs won two titles each. The final returned to London in 2008, where [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] became the first side to win the competition at the new Wembley, beating Chelsea 2–1 after extra time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Jonathan |last=Stevenson |title=Tottenham 2–1 Chelsea |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7256729.stm |work=BBC Sport |publisher=BBC |date=24 February 2008 |access-date=30 January 2009 |archive-date=25 February 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080225134253/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/7256729.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>
